title: Leadership and Background
subtitle: Attolloo Group is founded and led by Nils Johan Brede. The method draws on four decades of work in technology, security and leadership in regulated markets.

sections.heading: Four Decades, Five Shifts
sections.body:
The competitive advantage I bring to Attolloo is not primarily methodological. It is experiential. Every framework in the Attolloo methodology stack was distilled from something I encountered, solved, and internalised in an operating role — across five distinct generations of technology disruption in regulated markets.

GENERATION 1 — THE INFRASTRUCTURE PROBLEM (1980-1996)
I completed a cand.mag. degree in informatics and economics at the University of Oslo in 1983.

+++ More on this period

Moving through defence, management consulting, enterprise computing, and technology commercialisation across the following decade, I encountered the same pattern repeatedly: large technology projects do not fail on the technology. They fail on governance and human absorption capacity. Every major AI adoption survey in 2026 confirms this is still true. The pattern has not changed. The technology has.

+++

GENERATION 2 — DIGITAL PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE (1996-1999)
As CEO of Lokalnett AS from 1996 to 1999, I led the build-out of some of Norway's first municipal internet portals for more than 30 municipalities, with A-pressen as investor.

+++ More on this period

There was no reference case, no established methodology, and no precedent for how a public institution — governed by democratic accountability, political stakeholders, and regulatory constraint — should engage with a new digital infrastructure layer. I had to create that methodology from scratch, under operational and political pressure, with real institutional accountability. The challenge of deploying AI in a public or regulated institutional context in 2026 is structurally identical. I have been in that room before.

+++

GENERATION 3 — REGULATORY COMPLIANCE AS BUSINESS ARCHITECTURE (2000-2008)
Working in senior advisory roles in the early 2000s, I developed deep fluency in regulatory compliance not as a legal overhead, but as business architecture — leading e-government implementation and regulatory compliance work across more than 100 Norwegian municipalities.

+++ More on this period

The core insight that would later underpin the Kando Framework emerged here: regulatory pressure is not a constraint on innovation. It is a forcing function that, correctly structured, produces more durable and scalable business models. In 2003 I founded one of Norway's first e-marketing programmes, formally opened by the Minister of Trade in March 2004.

+++

GENERATION 4 — CYBERSECURITY, TURNAROUND, AND EUROPEAN REGULATORY SCALE (2014-2019)
As CEO of Watchcom Security Group from 2014 to 2016, I led an operational turnaround under financial pressure that ended with the sale of the company to a major defence and security group.

+++ More on this period

For founders in difficulty, this is the proof point that matters most: I have done this in crisis mode, not just in growth mode. As Director in PwC's cyber and risk practice from 2017 to 2019, I led Privacy Tech implementation at European scale — GDPR and MiFID II for clients across the European market, during the period when those frameworks were being written, interpreted, and first enforced. The EU AI Act is now where GDPR was in 2018: in force, still being interpreted, and with its obligations phasing in. I navigated that first enforcement cycle from the inside, for real clients, under real pressure.

+++

GENERATION 5 — AI GOVERNANCE IN PRACTICE (2019-PRESENT)
Since 2019 I have served in a dual executive role at one of Norway's most complex regulated public institutions — holding security, privacy, and data governance on one axis, and people and organisational leadership on the other, simultaneously, reporting to the chief executive.

+++ More on this period

I operate that integrated model as a permanent governance structure. The AI Compass diagnostic draws on the general experience of operating such a model.

+++

NOTE ON INTEGRITY
All Attolloo activities are conducted with strict separation from other executive responsibilities. No information, processes, or relationships from current institutional roles are used in any commercial Attolloo context. This boundary is a foundational principle, not a preference. Attolloo does not take on companies that compete in the pension market, companies whose main customers are pension providers or the public sector, or companies that supply, or are bidding to supply, my current employer.

sections.heading: Academic Foundation
sections.body:
I completed the MBA & Master in Digital Business at ENEB in Barcelona in August 2026, a programme of seventeen modules certified by Universidad Isabel I. I took the programme late in my career for a practical reason: to check what I had learned in practice against the current literature, and to be made to write the method down.

Before that: a cand.mag. degree in informatics and economics from the University of Oslo, and a one-year programme in organisation and leadership at HiNT.

The frameworks came from practice first and were connected to theory afterwards. They have not been independently validated. The [Research](/research.html) page sets out what that would take.

sections.heading: Why Attolloo Exists
sections.body:
Most early-stage AI companies in regulated sectors can find capital. What they often cannot find is someone with executive experience in security, privacy and regulated markets who can tell them what a buyer, a regulator or an investor will ask for.

That is what I offer: first as a defined assessment for a fee, and for a few companies as a longer partnership with equity. The aim is that the governance stays in the company when I leave.
